x.Liquefaction Capacity & Utilization: Total nameplate liquefaction capacity (mtpa) and actual utilization rates. High capacity and utilization indicate strong operational scale and efficiency.
x.Feedstock Supply Security: Access to reliable natural gas feedstocks, including long-term supply agreements and upstream integration. Secure feedstock ensures stable operations and cost control.
x.Asset Reliability & Uptime: Track record of plant availability, on-stream time, and maintenance performance. High uptime minimizes production losses and maximizes revenue.
x.Safety & Regulatory Compliance: Safety performance (e.g., TRIR) and adherence to environmental and operational regulations. Strong compliance reduces operational risk and enhances reputation.
x.Carbon Intensity & Efficiency: Greenhouse gas emissions per tonne of LNG produced and energy efficiency of liquefaction trains. Lower carbon intensity improves market access and meets decarbonization goals.

y.LNG Sales & Contract Portfolio: Volume of LNG contracted under long-term and spot agreements, including contract duration and pricing terms. A robust portfolio ensures revenue stability and market presence.
y.Customer & Geographic Diversification: Spread of customers across regions and markets. Diversification reduces dependence on any single buyer or region, mitigating demand risk.
y.Financial Performance & Liquidity: Revenue, EBITDA, cash flow, and debt metrics. Strong financials enable investment in growth and resilience to market volatility.
y.Growth Project Pipeline: Planned or under-construction liquefaction and regasification projects, including capacity additions and timelines. A robust pipeline indicates future growth potential.
y.Strategic Partnerships & Market Position: Joint ventures, equity stakes, and long-term supply deals with major players. Strong partnerships enhance market access and competitive positioning.

xy_scoring.axis_definition_reason: These parameters capture the core drivers of success in the global LNG market: operational excellence in liquefaction and supply security, combined with commercial strength in contracting, diversification, and financial resilience. They are specific to LNG's asset-heavy, long-term contract nature.
